subject: BlueWave QBR — advance briefing: health snapshot, renewal risks & exec asks
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: BlueWave QBR — advance briefing: health snapshot, renewal risks & exec asks

Team —

BlueWave's QBR is scheduled for 2028-04-25 (customer requested an exec presence). I pulled together a concise pre-brief with the current account health signals and a prioritized renewal risk register. Key items below; full notes and the draft deck attached.

Quick headline: Account is medium risk. Usage is stable but several factors increase churn probability unless we act before the QBR:
- Product adoption: steady token volumes but 3 power users dropped usage last month (see usage CSV).
- Recent latency incidents (early March) were mitigated but the customer flagged them in their internal postmortem and asks for improved SLA language.
- Pricing sensitivity: procurement opened a dialog to renegotiate seat/throughput tiers for 2029.

Top 6 renewal risks (prioritized):
1) SLA / latency perception — customer wants clearer SLOs and credit language (Elena explicitly asked for this).
2) Cost per token concerns — procurement comparing our numbers vs a hosted competitor.
3) Executive sponsor churn — their VP of Data (Doug Reynolds) hinted at renewed interest in an alternative stack.
4) Missing product roadmap items (multimodal connectors) that BlueWave expects in H2.
5) Contract timing — procurement delaying signature until after their internal budget review (May).
6) Onboarding for new analytics team — requires dedicated onboarding hours (we're short).

Recommended exec asks for the QBR (for leadership to authorize ahead of time):
- Approve a one-time 10% promotional credit tied to meeting the end-of-Q2 adoption milestone (to neutralize price pushback).
- Commit a short SLA addendum and offer a 90-day trial of expanded latency monitoring for BlueWave’s critical routes.
- Assign a senior pre-sales SE to lead the H2 connector feasibility session.

Attachments: bluewave-qbr-draft-deck.pdf, renewal-risk-registry.xlsx, customer-usage-trends.csv

Action items for this thread: please reply with: (1) who will own the SLA addendum language; (2) confirm if we can approve the promotional credit; (3) who will present exec asks on the call.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: bluewave-qbr-draft-deck.pdf (PDF, 220KB)]
[Attachment: renewal-risk-registry.xlsx (Spreadsheet, 95KB)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave QBR — advance briefing: health snapshot, renewal risks & exec asks

Nikhil — thanks for the concise rundown, this is exactly what I needed. A few clarifications and requests:

1) SLA addendum: I can draft the initial language but will need legal to sign off. Can we scope it to: (a) clarified P95 latency by model class, (b) limited credit schedule capped at 3% of annual committed spend, and (c) a 90-day observability pilot? That should be enough to reassure them without exposing the business.

2) Promotional credit: I'm OK with the 10% as a one-off contingent on hitting the adoption milestone — but need a quick ROI note. If the deal closes for next year at current commitment, what's the expected payback? Please include a short line in the deck that shows conservative payback.

3) Presentation: I'll take the executive asks if Karthik endorses the OKR tie-in (see below). I will also add a one-slide risk heatmap to the draft deck.

4) Please add a short customer quote or artifact showing positive outcomes (we have the case note from Feb where BlueWave reported a 2x speedup on report generation). Marissa — can you surface that in the deck?

I'll queue legal review for the SLA language once you send the proposed text.

- Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: renewal-risk-registry.xlsx (updated comments)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave QBR — advance briefing: health snapshot, renewal risks & exec asks

Adding account-level color from CS side:

- Customer sentiment: overall positive with operational concerns. Elena has been responsive but pragmatic. Doug (VP Data) is the wildcard — he respects the engineering team but is budget conservative.
- Usage detail: the three power users who dropped were on an ad-hoc analytics cohort; one returned after we suggested query-level caching. The other two cited headcount changes.
- Recent incidents: we ran a remediation and increased cache TTLs; they saw improvement. The customer still wants a more proactive RCA cadence.
- Onboarding ask: BlueWave is requesting 40 hours of dedicated enablement across Apr–May for their new analytics hires. We can offer 25 hours standard; recommend we approve +15 hours as a chargeable, discounted block or include it as a one-time service credit.

Suggested language to add to the deck: "Operational stability improvements completed; recommending a 90-day observability pilot and an enablement package to accelerate adoption."

I'll attach a short excerpt from our February success note.

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: feb-success-note-BlueWave.txt (text, 6KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueWave QBR — advance briefing: health snapshot, renewal risks & exec asks

Thanks — solid triage. A couple of points from an OKR and product-program perspective:

- OKR alignment: this account maps to Q2 Objective "Improve retention among top-10 accounts by 5%". If we make the observability pilot and the enablement package contingent on specific adoption metrics, we can count successful remediation toward that key result.
- Credit ask: approve the one-time 10% promotional credit only if we get a signed commitment for the 2029 baseline within 30 days post-QBR (legal to include this clause). This reduces open-ended discounts.
- Presentation: I can join the QBR to speak to product roadmap items and feasibility of the requested connectors. I'll need a 20-minute slot.

I'll add a short slide linking the customer ask to our OKRs and include the conditional credit language. Nikhil/Lauren — if you confirm the adoption milestone we can lock the clause.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: BlueWave QBR — advance briefing: health snapshot, renewal risks & exec asks

Perfect — thanks all. Quick confirmations: 

- SLA addendum: Lauren will draft; Nikhil to circulate to legal by EOD 4/12.
- Promotional credit: approved conditionally per Karthik's note — 10% one-time credit contingent on signed baseline within 30 days after QBR. Finance to confirm language.
- Enablement hours: Marissa to propose a packaged option (25 included + 15 discounted) and a billable alternative; include pricing in slide 6.
- Presentation: Lauren will present exec asks; Karthik will cover roadmap feasibility (20 min); I will own renewal commercial ask and negotiation plan.

Next steps: I'll set a 30-minute pre-brief for 4/20 11:00am PT to finalize the deck and run through the ask script. Elena/Doug — looping you to confirm that date/time works for your team; if not, please propose an alternative.

Regards,
Nikhil
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
